summary: Round 2 re-review from scratch. The round-1 blocker (horn proxy sitting on the spline tip) is fixed: horn face is 0.8 mm above the spline top, and the tilt-axis, wall_out and horn_y chain is consistent with the catalog (SG90 shaft_h 7.6, tab_t 2.4, horn hub 4.0 / spline_engage 3.2). All requirement checks pass with margin (pan +/-90, tilt -35..+65, torque 2% of stall, FEA 1-2.6 MPa against 13 MPa, deflection 0.22 of 0.3 mm on the yoke, sweeps clear, mass 59 g). The FEA hot spots sit where the load path puts them (horn contact and standoff holes on the bracket, tilt window corners and wall root on the yoke, tab pilots on the base). The remaining risks are the estimated horn dimensions and a few small fit and print details, all minor.

findings.issue: Pan-horn screws are M2 x 8 through the 6 mm plate, so they engage only 2.0 mm in a horn disc that the catalog lists as an UNVERIFIED 2.0 mm estimate. That is 1 d of thread in aluminium and the tip ends flush. If the real disc is thinner, the thread is short.
findings.fix: Measure the purchased horn. Keep the M2 x 8 only if the disc is at least 2 mm thick; otherwise reduce yoke_t to 5 or add a thin shim, then update the catalog value.

findings.issue: Tilt horn screws are M2 x 6 through the 3.5 mm arm, giving 2.5 mm into the same estimated 2 mm disc. The tips protrude about 0.5 mm toward the servo boss. Clearance is fine in the model, but it depends on the estimated hub depth.
findings.fix: Verify with the real horn. If the hub is shallower than assumed, use M2 x 5 or recheck the clearance to the servo boss.

findings.issue: The servo-lead slot is only 4.7 mm wide with a 1.3 mm wall to the tab pilot. An SG90 three-wire flat lead with its connector housing may not fit through it, and the 1.3 mm wall will not take a rough fit. The pilots are printed M2 threads, good for only a few cycles (already noted in DESIGN.md).
findings.fix: Print the base first and test-fit the lead. If tight, open the slot to about 6 mm or route the lead over the end wall. Consider M2 heat-set inserts for the tab pilots if the servo will be removed often.

findings.issue: The yoke needs support or bridging at the tilt-servo window, which has a 12.8 mm top bridge, plus the ledge slots and the FPC notch. The part sheet shows ragged window edges at the top of the +Y wall. The overhang is flagged only as 1.9%, but the bridge quality decides how the servo case seats.
findings.fix: Check the sliced preview of the window. Add a 0.2 mm sacrificial layer or enable bridge-flow tuning, and ream the window to size if it sags.

findings.issue: Slicer warning: 3.5% of the surface needs support. The cause is the teardrop and 45-degree holes and the horizontal horn-key access holes (2.4 mm). The small 2.4 mm teardrop holes may close up or leave strings, so the 1.5 mm key may not pass cleanly.
findings.fix: Ream the 2.4 mm key-access holes with a 2.5 mm drill after printing, and say so in ASSEMBLY.md.

findings.issue: No electrical: block (kerf warning). Servo power and signal, the 5 V supply and bulk capacitor (A6), and the lead strain relief are described in prose only. The tilt servo lead is tied to the yoke and then dangles to the base without a strain relief at the pan axis; with +/-90 deg pan it twists around the horn.
findings.fix: Add the electrical block (servo pair 5 V >= 1 A, 470-1000 uF). Specify a loose lead loop at the pan axis of at least 60 mm, like the FPC, in ASSEMBLY.md.

findings.issue: The tripod screw protrusion window of 5.5-8 mm (A2) is an assumption, and a longer screw would hit the pan servo only 2 mm above an 8 mm tip. The 40 x 26 mm footprint is small for a head that sits 13 mm off-centre on a 70 mm tall stack, so a tall tripod screw or a loose joint could tip it.
findings.fix: Keep the warning in the instructions. Consider a printed 3 mm skirt or a wider base if it will sit on soft surfaces.
